body: Local-first screen and audio memory that records what you see and hear, then lets you and your AI agents search it with natural language.
commercial_use_note: Allowed with the required commercial license.
offline_note: Raw capture is stored locally by default. Configured cloud AI, transcription, sync, integrations and connected AI clients can transmit context off-device. Offline availability depends on the selected components and configuration.
history_note: Stores captured screen and audio history locally; configured sync and integrations may transmit context off-device.
plain_description: Screenpipe gives you a searchable memory of everything you see and hear on your computer, so you never lose a meeting detail, tab, or idea again. It quietly records your screen and audio on your own machine, then answers plain questions like what you worked on today or what was said in a call. Source code is available for specified personal non-commercial uses; commercial or production use, including official desktop builds, requires a paid plan — see https://screenpipe.com/onboarding.
technical_description: Screenpipe is a Rust and TypeScript desktop app built with Tauri that captures screen and audio locally into SQLite with full-text search. Event-driven capture stores screenshots with the OS accessibility tree and falls back to OCR, while Whisper runs on-device for transcription with speaker diarization (a cloud transcription option is also available). A local REST API, MCP server (see https://github.com/screenpipe/screenpipe/tree/main/packages/screenpipe-mcp), and JavaScript SDK let agents like Claude Code or Cursor query history, and markdown pipes run scheduled automations with deterministic per-pipe data permissions. Raw capture is stored locally by default; configured cloud AI, transcription, sync, integrations and connected AI clients can transmit context off-device. Privacy filters redact passwords and PII at rest with optional encryption. Product analytics and crash diagnostics are on by default and can be switched off in settings. The source is source-available for specified personal non-commercial use (see https://github.com/screenpipe/screenpipe/blob/main/LICENSE.md); commercial or production use, including official desktop builds, needs a paid license — see https://screenpipe.com/onboarding.
